analysis:
The only change is in scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py, head lines 180-182, in test_only_the_release_lane_compiles_the_release_environment. The old assertion forbade any DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT in the qualify-sdk job. The new one forbids the resolved-environment selector in qualify-sdk (needs.resolve-env.outputs.environment) and requires exactly one literal assignment of `prod` there. This is a CI guard test only. It ships no runtime or provider code and touches no coordinator, provider, attestation or key paths.

Security effect: the test now pins the qualification lane to a fixed compile-time environment of `prod`, so it cannot drift to the resolved environment. That is a reasonable tightening. The test does not verify that qualify-sdk really sets the value to `prod`. It only checks the workflow text, which the PR changes elsewhere (release-provider.yml and the action are outside this batch).

Remaining integration question: whether release-provider.yml's qualify-sdk job actually carries `DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod`, and whether compiling the qualification lane as prod has any effect on signing or publication. The qualify-sdk job is asserted to hold no secrets and to have no environment, and the signing job's smoke checks compare against ENV_PREFIX. I found no regression in this file. The canonical threat model scope (TB-009/TB-011 attestation/build-qualification, T-034, T-054) is not weakened by this test change. The workflow files themselves were not in this batch, so they are not covered.
